$comment: Authored port of the hand-written registry group iam-roles (docs/plans/compat-coverage-modelgen.md §3.11, #1116). One spec in place of the six per-language implementations of that group, and of the one that was never written — rust-sdk carries 16 rows of compat/parity-debt.json for it, which the port closes. It runs as iam-roles-shadow (candidate, shadowOf: iam-roles) beside the natives until the nightly comparison agrees; this file flips nothing. The clauses are the union of what the six natives assert — see compat/model/README.md § Authored scenarios. Every policy document is compared with `equalsJSON` (#2179): botocore hands python-sdk and cli a decoded object where the other five backends hold the percent-encoded string, so no `equals` could hold in both, and none of the natives compared a document by value at all.

groups.$comment: Two roles. `role` is the group's own: CreateRole makes it with the fixture tags, and every later test reads or mutates it — which is what node-js-sdk, java-sdk and cli do. `doomed` is a bare role setup makes for DeleteRole to remove, which is what go-sdk, python-sdk and dotnet-sdk do (each creates and deletes a role of its own inside that test). The split is forced by the schedule: DeleteRole is listed twelfth in the registry, ahead of the four inline-policy tests that still need `role`, and runs last only because the loaders topologically sort `depends` (it depends on DeleteRolePolicy). Deleting `doomed` makes the group correct in file order as well as in dependency order, and it removes a role with nothing attached, so AWS has no DeleteConflict to raise — node-js-sdk, java-sdk and cli first had to take `role` out of the instance profile with unchecked calls, which a scenario test cannot make. `role`'s attachments, its instance profile and the role itself go in teardown, in the order AWS requires. Nothing is exported but the role's ARN: IAM names are the handles, and `$name` makes them.
groups.name: iam-roles-shadow

tests.$comment: All six natives trust lambda.amazonaws.com. node-js-sdk and java-sdk create the group's role here with the fixture tags (owner=compat, stage=dev, the set every native tags with); go-sdk, python-sdk and dotnet-sdk create it in setup and make a throwaway role in this test instead; cli creates it here and asserts nothing about the response. The union of the assertions: RoleId (node-js-sdk, java-sdk) and Arn (java-sdk, dotnet-sdk) present, RoleName the one asked for (python-sdk), and the role listed by ListRoles (dotnet-sdk). ListRoles asks for MaxItems 1000 as java-sdk does, so a busy account's first page of 100 cannot hide the role. IAM is eventually consistent, so the listing goes through `eventually` with the generated iam recipe's budget (6 × 500 ms); no native polls, and Overcast answers on the first attempt.
tests.name: CreateRole

tests.$comment: All six natives send the same malformed trust policy — a statement with no Action or NotAction, which the IAM User Guide says AWS refuses — and require MalformedPolicyDocument. That is the awsQueryError code the model gives MalformedPolicyDocumentException, so the clause carries both spellings. The six natives also require HTTP 400, which the IR cannot state: it has no status-code check. The model binds this error to 400 (`smithy.api#httpError`), but that half of the assertion is not carried over. No depends, as in the registry. Teardown deletes the `malformed` role in case a regression stored it, as node-js-sdk, dotnet-sdk and cli do.
tests.name: CreateRoleMalformedDocument

tests.$comment: go-sdk, python-sdk, java-sdk and dotnet-sdk assert RoleName; node-js-sdk and dotnet-sdk assert that Arn is present; cli asserts nothing. The union pins the ARN to the one CreateRole returned, which is stronger than present. The trust policy is compared by value with `equalsJSON` — no native read it back. The IAM API reference documents it on the Role that GetRole returns, as a URL-encoded document.
tests.name: GetRole

tests.$comment: All six natives agree: both fixture tags come back on the role GetRole returns, which is where the API reference documents them (API_Role.html). One listContains per tag, as each native checks the two independently.
tests.name: GetRoleReturnsTags

tests.$comment: python-sdk, node-js-sdk, java-sdk and dotnet-sdk require the group's role in the listing; go-sdk and cli only that the call succeeds. Membership is the union. MaxItems 1000 is java-sdk's; the others take the default page of 100, which a busy account can fill.
tests.name: ListRoles

tests.$comment: The natives disagree on the managed policy: go-sdk and python-sdk attach arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/ReadOnlyAccess, while node-js-sdk, java-sdk, cli and dotnet-sdk attach AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess. This file uses the majority's. go-sdk also attaches it to a role of its own that it creates here, not to the group's role. No native asserts anything beyond success. The read-back is the check ListAttachedRolePolicies makes next, run through `eventually` (6 × 500 ms, the iam recipe's budget) because IAM is eventually consistent.
tests.name: AttachRolePolicy

tests.$comment: python-sdk, node-js-sdk, java-sdk and dotnet-sdk require the attached policy's ARN in the listing; go-sdk and cli only that the call succeeds. Membership is the union.
tests.name: ListAttachedRolePolicies

tests.$comment: No native asserts anything beyond success. The detach is proved the way the attach was: the policy is gone from ListAttachedRolePolicies, polled for the same reason and with the same budget.
tests.name: DetachRolePolicy

tests.$comment: python-sdk and java-sdk assert InstanceProfileName; dotnet-sdk asserts that Arn is present; go-sdk, node-js-sdk and cli assert nothing. node-js-sdk, java-sdk and cli also accept EntityAlreadyExists from an earlier run against the same emulator. A `$name` is scoped to the run, so this test does not need that. The union pins the name and requires the ARN.
tests.name: CreateInstanceProfile

tests.$comment: No native asserts anything beyond success here; GetInstanceProfile checks the membership next. The read-back makes the same check here, through `eventually` with the iam recipe's budget.
tests.name: AddRoleToInstanceProfile

tests.$comment: python-sdk and java-sdk assert the profile's name; python-sdk, node-js-sdk and dotnet-sdk assert that the group's role is in its Roles; go-sdk asserts only that InstanceProfile is present; cli asserts nothing. The union checks both the name and the role.
tests.name: GetInstanceProfile

tests.$comment: python-sdk and dotnet-sdk create a role, delete it, and require it gone from ListRoles; go-sdk creates and deletes one and asserts only success; node-js-sdk, java-sdk and cli delete the group's own role after unchecked calls that clear its instance profile. Here the role is `doomed`, which setup made — see the group's $comment for why. The union: absent from ListRoles (MaxItems 1000, as above), and GetRole answering NoSuchEntity, which is the error the IAM API reference names for a role that does not exist. Both go through `eventually` with the iam recipe's budget, because IAM is eventually consistent. depends mirrors registry.json exactly.
tests.name: DeleteRole

tests.$comment: The natives disagree on both the policy name and the document. java-sdk names the policy `inline`, and the other five name it inline-role-policy. The document grants logs:* in node-js-sdk and dotnet-sdk, s3:GetObject in go-sdk and python-sdk, s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject in cli, and s3:ListAllMyBuckets in java-sdk. This file uses inline-role-policy and dotnet-sdk's logs:* document, because dotnet-sdk is the only native that reads the document back and checks it (for logs:*). No native asserts anything beyond success here. The read-back compares the stored document by value, polled with the iam recipe's budget.
tests.name: PutRolePolicy

tests.$comment: python-sdk asserts PolicyName. go-sdk, node-js-sdk and java-sdk assert that PolicyDocument is present, and dotnet-sdk that its decoded text contains logs:*. cli asserts nothing. The union pins PolicyName and RoleName, which the IAM API reference documents on the GetRolePolicy response, and compares the document by value with `equalsJSON`. That is stronger than both present and contains.
tests.name: GetRolePolicy

tests.$comment: All six natives agree: the policy's name is in PolicyNames.
tests.name: ListRolePolicies

tests.$comment: No native asserts anything beyond success. The delete is proved by the name leaving ListRolePolicies, polled with the iam recipe's budget.
tests.name: DeleteRolePolicy
